narration.en: A young coriander plant and a flowering one have leaves of quite different shapes. A cell can also go back to dividing after it has matured. Plants are remarkably flexible.

body.en: Cells derived from root and shoot apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions; this is differentiation. During it, cells undergo major structural changes in their walls and protoplasm. For example, to form a tracheary element the cells lose their protoplasm and develop a very strong, elastic lignocellulosic secondary wall to carry water over long distances. Living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain it under certain conditions; this is dedifferentiation, e.g. the formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells. The cells produced by such meristems again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions; this is redifferentiation.

points.en: Differentiation: tracheary elements lose protoplasm and develop lignified walls.
Dedifferentiation: interfascicular and cork cambium from parenchyma.
Redifferentiation: products of dedifferentiated meristems mature again.
Growth in plants is open and differentiation is also open.

narration.en: Plants follow different paths of development in response to the environment or to their stage of life: this is plasticity. In buttercup the leaves under water are finely dissected while those in air are broad. In coriander (and cotton, larkspur) the leaves of the young plant differ in shape from those of the mature plant. Both are heterophylly.
narration.kn: ಪರಿಸರ ಅಥವಾ ಜೀವನದ ಹಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಅನುಗುಣವಾಗಿ ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಮಾರ್ಗ ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ: ಇದು ನಮ್ಯತೆ. ಬಟರ್‌ಕಪ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೀರಿನೊಳಗಿನ ಎಲೆಗಳು ಸೀಳಿದ್ದು ಗಾಳಿಯಲ್ಲಿರುವವು ಅಗಲವಾಗಿವೆ. ಕೊತ್ತಂಬರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಎಳೆಯ ಸಸ್ಯದ ಎಲೆಗಳು ಪ್ರೌಢ ಸಸ್ಯದ ಎಲೆಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಭಿನ್ನ. ಎರಡೂ ಭಿನ್ನಪರ್ಣತೆ.

narration.en: Let us draw the cycle of differentiation and then two kinds of heterophylly.

say.en: Cells from meristems differentiate: they mature and specialise, like tracheary elements that lose their protoplasm and build lignified walls.
Living mature cells can regain the power to divide. That is dedifferentiation: parenchyma forms the interfascicular cambium and cork cambium.
The cells these new meristems produce mature again and lose the ability to divide: redifferentiation.
Plants show plasticity. In coriander, cotton and larkspur the juvenile leaves differ in shape from the mature ones.
In buttercup the leaves in air are broad, but the leaves under water are finely divided. Here the environment shapes the leaf.

Cells from a meristem mature into a sieve tube
Parenchyma between bundles forms interfascicular cambium
Explant cells form a callus in tissue culture
Cambium cells mature into secondary xylem and phloem
Callus cells form shoots and roots of a plantlet
Cork cambium cells mature into cork cells

explanation.en: Differentiation is maturing to do a special job. Dedifferentiation is a living, mature cell regaining the power to divide. Redifferentiation is the mature cells formed by such a meristem losing that power again.

body.en: Development is the sequence of events that occur in the life of a cell or an organism from germination of the seed to senescence. Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures; this ability is plasticity. Heterophylly is an example: in cotton, coriander and larkspur, the leaves of the juvenile plant differ in shape from those of the mature plant. In buttercup, leaves produced in air differ from those produced in water; here heterophylly is caused by the environment. Development is considered the sum of growth and differentiation, and it is under the control of intrinsic factors (genetic and intracellular, such as plant growth regulators) and extrinsic factors (light, temperature, water, oxygen, nutrition).

points.en: Heterophylly by life phase: cotton, coriander, larkspur.

problem.en: Classify each process: (a) a parenchyma cell in the cortex starts dividing to form cork cambium; (b) cells cut off by the cork cambium mature into cork cells; (c) a cambial derivative becomes a vessel element with a lignified wall.

steps.en: (a) A mature cell regaining the capacity to divide: dedifferentiation.
(b) Cells from a dedifferentiated meristem maturing for a specific function: redifferentiation.
(c) A meristem-derived cell maturing and losing its protoplasm: differentiation.
